name: pd_brick
title: PD Brick - USB-C PD programmable bench supply, 1.2-22 V
brief: USB-C Power Delivery programmable bench supply: an STUSB4500 PD sink negotiates up to 20 V and closes a P-FET load switch; an LM5176 4-switch buck-boost with four CSD18563Q5A FETs makes 1.2-22 V, set over I2C by an MCP4725 DAC injecting into its feedback node; an INA228 on a 10 mOhm shunt reads output voltage, current, power and energy; a high-side N-FET switch (gate rail from an MT3608 boost) enables the output onto a screw terminal; an ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 runs it all with Wi-Fi remote control, native USB on the same USB-C port, an I2C OLED header, a push-button rotary encoder and status LEDs; 3.3 V comes from an AP63203 buck off VBUS.

blocks.title: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 (Wi-Fi, native USB)
blocks.why: GPIOs on the module's right column (pins 27-40) and bottom row (15-26), the two sides that face the rest of the board; the left column only carries USB D-/D+ (13/14) to the receptacle below. Strapping pins IO3, IO45 and IO46 stay free.

netClasses.name: PWR_HI
netClasses.why: power path from the VBUS switch through the buck-boost to the terminal. IPC-2221 for 1.2 mm, 1 oz outer: 2.7 A at 10 C rise, 3.7 A at 20 C; on 0.5 oz inner copper only about 1.1 A, so these nets must stay on the outer layers (see README). Every pad on these nets is a power pad; IC sense pins hang off them through resistors.

netClasses.name: VBUS_IN
netClasses.why: receptacle VBUS: the HRO receptacle's VBUS pads are 0.6 mm wide, 0.2 mm from the GND pad on one side and 0.25 mm from the SBU pad on the other, so with neckdown off no class wider than about 0.6 mm can enter them (a 1.2 mm class cannot reach the pads). Each VBUS pad pair gets its own 0.6 mm track to Q1's source pad (about 2.2 A each at a 20 C rise, outer); board.keepouts keep the two feeds apart. Clearance 0.15 mm (the board's, ample for 20 V): at 0.2 mm a 0.6 mm track had a 0.05 mm window to leave the A4/B9 pad and Freerouting left that pad pair unrouted

netClasses.name: BUCK_SW
netClasses.why: the AP63203's switch node (SW to the inductor and the bootstrap cap): 0.8 mm is about 2.8 A at a 20 C rise on 1 oz outer copper, above the regulator's 2 A, and still enters the TSOT-23-6 SW pin (0.6 mm pad, 0.95 mm pitch: 0.25 mm to the GND and BST pins beside it). The inductor and caps are locked tight to the IC, so the node is short

netClasses.name: RAIL_3V3
netClasses.why: the 3V3 trunk from the buck's output caps to the module and the logic: 0.3 mm is about 1.4 A at a 20 C rise on 1 oz outer copper, against well under 1 A of load; it still enters the INA228's 0.3 mm TSSOP pin at 0.15 mm. No current budget, so the ladder may narrow it if it ever leaves a connection open

netClasses.name: GATEDRV
netClasses.why: gate-drive loops of the LM5176: 0.3 mm: wider than signal tracks for lower inductance, narrow enough to leave a 0.65 mm-pitch HTSSOP pin between its neighbours

netClasses.name: ANALOG
netClasses.why: the LM5176's analog control nodes, kept slightly wider than signals; no current budget, so the ladder may narrow them to 0.2 mm (its narrow rung re-routes the board when one of them is open)

rules.why_rules: 0.15 mm track and clearance, 0.45 / 0.2 mm vias, inside the DFM profile (0.09 mm space, 0.15 mm drill): more routing channels, because at 0.2 mm / 0.5 mm full rebuilds of this board left 1-4 connections open
rules.why_min_hole: the ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 footprint's own thermal vias are 0.2 mm; JLCPCB multilayer boards drill 0.2 mm
rules.why_min_track: carried from the S3 LiPo brief: Freerouting can neck a signal to 0.10 mm into a fine-pitch pin; JLCPCB multilayer builds 0.09 mm

board.notes: 4 layers: F.Cu / In1 GND plane / In2 routing / B.Cu. In1 is a Specctra power layer during routing; every leftover area is poured after routing measures 0 open.

keepouts.name: cc2_via_guard
keepouts.why: keeps a via off the strip beside the A9/B4 VBUS pad's exit (y = 40.45): on an earlier build Freerouting's CC2 fan-out via sat 0.7 mm from that line, closer than track half-width + clearance + via radius (0.3 + 0.2 + 0.225 mm), so that pad pair was left unrouted and the last mile joined it to the other pair's track. The strip stays clear of the VBUS track itself: the width floor will not widen a segment whose midpoint lies in a via keep-out

keepouts.name: vbus_a4_up_block
keepouts.why: no F.Cu track over the A4/B9 VBUS feed (y = 35.55): that pad pair's only F.Cu way out leads right to Q1's source pad. On a build without it, the A4/B9 pair ended up joined to the 3.3 V buck's input cap (a 5.1 mm last-mile track to C6.1) instead of to Q1, so its current would have reached Q1 through a long detour

keepouts.name: vbus_a4_via_ban
keepouts.why: no via on the A4/B9 feed either, so it cannot drop to an inner layer toward the buck

keepouts.name: vbus_split_box
keepouts.why: no F.Cu track in the box between the two receptacle VBUS feeds (the CC and USB lines via down before x = 10), so the A4/B9 feed cannot drop into the A9/B4 feed and share one 0.6 mm track to Q1

keepouts.name: vbus_split_wedge
keepouts.why: continues the box to Q1's source pad (left end at x = 13.11): one feed lands on the pad's top edge, the other on its bottom edge

mcu:U?.why: module top-left, antenna over the top edge, away from the power stage

usbpd:J?.why: USB-C on the back (left) edge, level with the power stage; plug seats with the shell 0.6 mm proud

term:J?.why: output terminal on the front (right) edge, level with the power stage, wire entry outward

usbpd:R3?.why: gate pull-up above Q1, out of the VBUS feeds' path (left to the shelves, the gate network landed between the receptacle and the source pad)

usbpd:R5?.why: gate-drain (Miller) resistor above Q1, beside the pull-up

usbpd:D?.why: VBUS TVS just below the receptacle

usbpd:U?.why: PD controller below the receptacle, CC traces short

buck3v3:U?.why: 3.3 V buck between the receptacle and the module (x from the left edge), locked with its five parts as one tight cell: IN/GND pins (3/4) face down to the input cap, SW (5) right to the inductor, BST (6) up to its cap

buck3v3:C1?.why: 10 uF input cap right under the IC, pad 1 (VBUS) under IN (pin 3) and pad 2 (GND) under GND (pin 4): the input loop is two 0.85 mm hops

buck3v3:L?.why: inductor against the IC's SW side, pad 1 level with the SW pin (2 mm centre to centre)

buck3v3:C2?.why: bootstrap cap above the IC: pad 1 over BST (pin 6), pad 2 over the inductor's SW pad

buck3v3:C3?.why: first 22 uF output cap under the inductor, standing: pad 1 (3V3) up, pad 2 (GND) down beside the input cap's GND pad, so the output loop closes beside the IC

buck3v3:C4?.why: second 22 uF output cap beside the first, pad 1 (3V3) 0.8 mm under the inductor's 3V3 pad; standing, the pair ends above Q1's courtyard

bbp:Q1?.why: buck high side (lock x from the board centre: x = 34): drain (VIN) left toward the input caps, source (SW1) right toward the inductor

bbp:Q2?.why: buck low side under it (x = 34): drain (SW1) up, source (CS) down toward the sense resistor

bbp:L?.why: inductor between the two half-bridges (x = 47), pad 1 (SW1) left

bbp:Q4?.why: boost high side (x = 59): source (SW2) left, drain (VOUT) right toward the output caps

bbp:Q3?.why: boost low side (x = 59): drain (SW2) up, source (CS) down

bbp:R?.why: current-sense resistor under the inductor (x = 47), between the two low-side sources

bbc:U?.why: controller under the power stage, turned so its gate-drive row faces up: SW1/HDRV1/BOOT1/LDRV1 under the buck leg (left), LDRV2/BOOT2/HDRV2/SW2 under the boost leg (right), control pins facing down

bbp:C5?.why: input bulk under the input ceramics, + pad (pin 1) to the right, toward the controller

bbp:C10?.why: output bulk above the output ceramics, out of the path the ISNS sense pair takes from the shunt down to the controller

mon:R1?.why: output shunt after the output ceramics (x = 67): pad 1 (VOUT) left toward the caps, pad 2 (VOUT_SH) right toward the output switch

mon:U?.why: INA228 below the shunt, beside the shared ISNS sense pair it reads

mon:R2?.why: INA228 VBUS resistor at the shunt's VOUT_SH side

osw:Q1?.why: output switch (x = 78): drain (VOUT_SH) left toward the shunt, source pins (OUT_P) right toward the terminal, gate at the top-right corner

osw:D1?.why: 12 V gate-source zener right of the gate: cathode (OUT_G) left, anode (OUT_P) right toward the terminal track

osw:Q2?.why: gate pull-down transistor above the output switch, not at the MCU

osw:R1?.why: gate pull-up (1M from VGATE) above the gate

bbc:R9?.why: FB bottom resistor beside the DAC, out of the crowded control-pin row

bbc:R7?.why: MODE resistor in an even 2.1 mm fan under the control-pin row (pin side up)

bbc:R6?.why: COMP series resistor in the fan

bbc:C6?.why: COMP zero cap under its resistor

bbc:C7?.why: COMP high-frequency cap in the fan

bbc:C11?.why: VOSNS cap to the right of the control row

bbc:C10?.why: ISNS filter cap to the right of the control row, beside pins 13-14

bbc:C1?.why: VIN-pin cap to the left of the control row

bbc:R2?.why: VISNS resistor (from the filtered VIN-pin node) to the left of the control row

osw:U?.why: gate-rail boost next to VIN (bottom left), so the wide VIN track stays short; only the thin 25.6 V gate rail crosses to the output FETs

usbpd:R2?.why: DISCH resistor at the switched VIN node; only the thin PD_DISCH net runs to the controller

bbc:R10?.why: EN pull-down next to the MCU pin that drives it, out of the crowded control-pin row

bbc:R1?.why: VIN-pin filter resistor at the input bulk + pad; BB_VINP runs thin to the IC and its 100 nF

bbc:R3?.why: SW1 sense resistor at the buck switch node; BB_SW1K runs thin to the IC

bbc:R4?.why: SW2 sense resistor at the boost switch node; BB_SW2K runs thin to the IC

bbc:R8?.why: FB top resistor at the output caps; the FB net runs thin to the IC

bbc:R15?.why: VOSNS resistor at the output caps

bbc:R13?.why: ISNS(+) filter resistor at the shunt's VOUT pad (Kelvin)

bbc:R14?.why: ISNS(-) filter resistor at the shunt's VOUT_SH pad (Kelvin)

bbc:R11?.why: CS filter resistor at the sense resistor's CS pad; BB_CSP runs thin to the IC

osw:R4?.why: MT3608 feed resistor at the input bulk's + pad; VG_IN runs thin to the boost

dac:U?.why: DAC beside the LM5176 FB pin (bottom row, right)

boot:SW?.why: BOOT on the top edge, right of the module's courtyard box (the module's courtyard, antenna keep-out included, spans x -4 to 44 and y down to 20.3; the silk stage keeps words off every courtyard box, so at x = 38 the BOOT word found no spot)

reset:SW?.why: RESET at the left edge just below the module's courtyard box, left of the 3.3 V buck: beside the module's EN pin (x = 5, y = 15) its RST word found no spot outside that box

led_pwr:D?.why: status LEDs along the top edge, 3.75 mm apart, words above them

led_pd:D?.why: status LEDs along the top edge

led_out:D?.why: status LEDs along the top edge

led_pwr:R?.why: each LED's resistor straight below it, so the space above stays free for the LED's word (left to the shelves, the PD LED's resistor took the spot above the OUT LED and its word found no place)

oled:J?.why: OLED header standing vertical (pin 1, GND, at the top) right of the LEDs: the silk stage writes a header's pin names beside each pin, which on a horizontal row land on the next pin (0 of 8 labels fitted)

oled:R1?.why: SCL pull-up right of the header, level with the SCL pin, clear of the pin labels on the left

oled:R2?.why: SDA pull-up right of the header, level with the SDA pin

enc:SW?.why: encoder top-right, under the user's hand

holes:H1?.why: corner hole (lock x is from the board centre), locked before any satellite can take the corner

usbpd:Q?.why: VBUS load switch beside the receptacle, locked so its source pad (pin 3, y = 38.28) sits level with the middle of the receptacle's two VBUS pad pairs (y = 35.55 and 40.45): each pair gets its own feed to it (8.6 and 7.5 mm on the final build); gate (pin 1) above, drain tab toward the input caps. Listed after the other locks so the power stage's satellites are placed first, as before. x = 19.25 is where the earlier at-target legalised it, clear of the input ceramics

route.why: the ladder narrows only classes without a current budget; the outline is stated, so it is never grown

switches.why: the output terminal's two pins marked by the net each lands on, beside each pin on the board side. silk.polarity tries spots 1.9-2.3 mm from each pin; on this terminal every one of them hits the pin's own 2.6 mm pad or the terminal's body outline (measured on the previous build), so no + / - was printed

captions.place_3d: KiCad's raytracer on the placed board: USB-C in on the left, the LM5176 power stage across the middle, the screw terminal out on the right, the ESP32-S3 antenna over the top edge.
captions.done_3d: STUSB4500 PD sink, LM5176 4-switch buck-boost, INA228 monitor, high-side N-FET output switch, ESP32-S3, OLED header, encoder.
